items.title: Scientists discover new jellyfish species in waters off Alicante in Spain
items.snippet: The Mediterranean Sea still holds species unknown to science. One of them is Copula lucentia, a tiny jellyfish measuring just a few millimeters. items.title: Heavy rain can more than double glacier speeds in Alaska
items.snippet: Glaciers are often thought of as unyielding blocks of ice that slowly carve out the landscape as they move downhill by gravity. But sometimes their slow crawl becomes a surge that sees them move orders of magnitude faster than their usual speed.

items.title: The introduction of a medieval public health system exposed the population to roundworm
items.snippet: Medieval health and sanitation efforts involved deliberate interventions; however, some of these measures had the opposite effect, leading to an increased spread of disease in Trondheim.

items.title: Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
items.snippet: An alternative model in which the universe is 26.7 billion years old and needs neither dark matter nor dark energy has held up against several major cosmology tests, according to a new University of Ottawa study. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," is published in the journal Universe.
items.source_name: Phys.org

items.title: Why treating soil acidity crop by crop is no longer enough for prairie farmers
items.snippet: To protect their future harvests, Western Canadian farmers need to manage soil acidity across their entire multiyear rotation rather than crop by crop, long-term research from the University of Alberta suggests.
